subject: Discovery recap: Dedicated GPU eligibility — constraints, success criteria, and next actions
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Kayla Morgan <kayla.morgan@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: Dedicated GPU eligibility — constraints, success criteria, and next actions

Hi Kayla — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call so we have aligned next steps. I pasted the key notes below and a short proposed pilot plan. Please correct anything I’ve captured incorrectly.

Pain points and goals
- Production latency spikes at peak trading windows (15–30s for long-context generation).
- Need guaranteed TPS for critical models: auth-flow ranking and long-context summarization.
- Data isolation requirement for PII-sensitive scoring (must be segregated from multi-tenant workloads).
- Cost predictability is important for forecasting next-quarter budgets.

Current stack
- Models: mixture of open LLMs (fin-tuned) and an internally maintained conversational model.
- Hosting: hybrid cloud; inference currently on bursty shared GPUs (Nvidia A10p).
- Orchestration: internal Kubernetes with custom autoscaler; sticky sessions for KV cache.

Success criteria for Dedicated fit
- Predictable steady-state TPS for core endpoints (>= 120 TPS aggregate).
- Isolation via reserved GPU pool with VPC peering.
- Autoscale with burst capacity to handle 3x baseline for 10–15 minute windows.
- End-to-end P95 latency <= 200ms for short responses, <= 3s for longer, streamed outputs.

Proposed pilot (recommended)
- 2-week reserved pool: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs, autoscale policy up to 12 GPUs for short bursts.
- Instrumentation: token-level cost telemetry and per-route latency tracing enabled.
- Success metrics: maintain 120 TPS steady-state, validate isolation via audit logs, and confirm cost per 1M tokens target.

Next steps
1) Kayla: share Ledgerly’s infra diagram and SRE contact (you mentioned ledgerly-devops@ledgerly.com) — I’ve attached an example stub for reference.
2) Redwood: circulate a concise pilot SOW + preliminary SLA draft for legal review (SLA_terms_draft.pdf).
3) Ops alignment call (internal + Ledgerly SRE) — propose Wed 2026-11-04 10:00 PT.

Thanks — I’ll queue the SOW and a short runbook for the pilot once I get the infra artifacts.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Dedicated GPU eligibility — constraints, success criteria, and next actions

Thanks Vivek — appreciate the recap. A few clarifications from our side: we do need hard isolation (no shared tenant compute for the PII scoring path) and audit log retention for 12 months. The 3x burst target is realistic but only for short bursts — typically 8–12 minutes during batch windows.

Attached a quick infra snapshot and our SRE list; the devops inbox is monitored by our on-call. Also: our procurement team will need the initial SOW and a clear list of what constitutes usage (how you meter tokens vs. node-hours).

One ask: can the pilot include a brief soak-test during our next batch window (Friday, 2026-11-06)? If Redwood can provision the burst policy by Thursday EOD, we can validate on Friday.

-Kayla
Lead ML Platform Engineer, Ledgerly

Kayla — thanks, that all makes sense and is helpful. Couple quick notes:
- We can enforce tenant isolation by allocating a dedicated reserved pool (no multi-tenant mapping) and provide KMS-integrated key separation.
- Audit logs: Redwood can retain operator/audit logs for 12 months for Private/Dedicated customers — I’ll include the retention config in the SOW.
- Burst policy: we can configure autoscale to allow 3x baseline for 10–15 minutes; to guarantee that we will need a short cold-start mitigation plan (warm-preload or KV priming).

Proposed immediate actions:
- I’ll draft the SOW + short-runbook today and share by EOD.
- Marissa, can you confirm ops capacity to approve a 2-week pilot with 4 baseline and 12 burst GPUs and lead the Friday soak test?

Cheers,
Vivek

Looping in internal ops notes for record and next steps.

Internal decision (ops): we can greenlight a 2-week pilot with the following guardrails:
- Baseline allocation: 4x A100-equivalent (reserved).
- Autoscale ceiling: 12 GPUs for max 15 minutes per burst; controller will enforce a 30-minute cooldown between bursts unless manually overridden.
- Isolation: dedicate the pool to Ledgerly with VPC peering and separate KMS key.
- Logging: enable 12-month retention and provide an export endpoint.

Procurement asks (I copied Ledgerly): please provide the procurement contact and PO cadence. We will send a short SOW + preliminary SLA (SLA_terms_draft.pdf) by EOD today; Kayla, we’ll include a clear usage definition (tokens vs node-hours) and a mini runbook for the Friday soak test.

I’ll also assign an Ops lead for the pilot and share a runbook link after Huddle.

-Marissa
